sections.content: A CROSS JOIN produces the Cartesian product of two tables — every row of table A paired with every row of table B, with no join condition. sections.label: Answer
sections.content: CROSS JOIN returns all possible row combinations (m × n rows) unconditionally, while INNER JOIN returns only the combinations that satisfy a specified matching condition between the tables.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **A fact table stores quantitative, measurable data (e.g., sales amount, quantity) tied to foreign keys of the dimensions, while dimension tables store descriptive, categorical context (e.g., product name, region, date)** used to slice and filter the facts.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the two-phase commit (2PC) protocol in distributed databases?
questions.title: What is the main purpose of the two-phase commit (2PC) proto
options: To ensure all participating nodes either commit or abort a transaction uniformly
To speed up read queries across replicas
To assign primary keys across shards
To compress log files during recovery
questions.answer: To ensure all participating nodes either commit or abort a transaction uniformly

sections.label: Theory
sections.content: 2PC coordinates a transaction spanning multiple database nodes (a coordinator + participants).

sections.label: Steps
sections.content:
1. Prepare phase: the coordinator asks all participants if they can commit; each replies yes/no.
2. Commit phase: only if ALL participants said yes does the coordinator tell everyone to commit; otherwise it tells everyone to abort.

sections.label: Answer
sections.content: **2PC ensures atomicity across multiple nodes — either every participating node commits the transaction, or all of them abort it**, preventing a state where some nodes committed and others didn't.
